blocks.text: After you have added an application segment with Privileged Remote Access (PRA), you can go to the Privileged Consoles page. For a complete list of ranges and limits per feature, see Ranges & Limitations.
When configuring a privileged portal within the Default Microtenant, you can link a maximum number of privileged consoles to the privileged portal. To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.
To learn more about PRA, see Understanding Privileged Remote Access. To set up PRA, see Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Privileged Remote Access.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Browser > Privileged Remote Access > Privileged Consoles.
Click Add.
The Add Console window appears.
In the Add Console window:
Console Type
On the Console Type tab, configure the following privileged console information:
Privileged Remote Access Portal: Select an existing portal(s) from the drop-down menu.

You can select both the Default Microtenant portal and the Microtenant portals that are assigned to the Microtenants. The portals that are assigned to the Microtenants are assigned by the Default Microtenant.
Privileged Remote Access Applications: Select an application(s) from the drop-down menu.

You can select applications from the Default Microtenant or from a shared Microtenant. When a privileged console created in a Microtenant uses an application segment inherited from the Default Microtenant, check with the Default Microtenant admin to confirm whether a privileged approval is required. For information on policy evaluation order, see Understanding Policies.
Click Next.
See image.
Consoles
On the Consoles tab, configure the following privileged console information:
Name: Enter a name for the privileged console. The name cannot contain special characters, with the exception of periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores ( _ ).
Display on Console: Enable to display the privileged console on the end user's Privileged Remote Access portal.
Protocol: Select the protocol type for the privileged console. The protocol types available are: VNC, RealVNC, SSH, and RDP.

If you select VNC or RealVNC and are enabling File Transfer in a consoles policy, the SFTP service needs to be enabled on the VNC or RealVNC server prior to creating the consoles policy, and the authentication for SFTP needs to match the VNC or RealVNC configuration. If SFTP is not configured, end users cannot connect to the privileged console.
SSH-enabled privileged consoles support modern elliptic-curve host algorithms (i.e., ecdsa-sha2-nistp521, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, and ecdsa-sha2-nistp256).
Domain: Enter a valid domain name.
Port: Enter the port number used for the privileged console.
Description: The description for the privileged console, if available.
Logo/Favicon: The logo represents if it is a VNC, RealVNC, SSH, or RDP connection.
Click Next.
See image.
Review
On the Review tab, review the console's configuration.
See image.
Click Save.
